items.title: Enabling zero trust: ALLEN’s move to Chrome Enterprise Premium
items.author: Rishabh ChhajerVice President – IT & CybersecurityALLEN Career Institute Pvt. Ltd.
items.content:
With a workforce that lives in the browser across a SaaS and multi-cloud estate, securing our digital environment is paramount. Our 5,000+ users include faculty, operations, engineering, contractors, and a large Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) population.

Operating at this scale, our top priority is protecting student personally identifiable information (PII) flowing through web applications. Under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), protecting this data is critical to regulatory compliance and maintaining brand trust. We needed security within the browser.

The challenge of a fragmented browser estate

We previously operated a mixed-browser environment, but managing multiple browsers made consistent policy enforcement and visibility challenging. We explored several options to standardize; however, our team didn’t want users to have to learn a new tool, and many of the options had high overhead costs.

Testing and rolling out Chrome Enterprise Premium

We implemented a phased Chrome Enterprise Premium pilot over a few weeks. Our team first validated the management capabilities in the Google Admin console by testing policy, deployment, extension controls, and reporting. Once we felt confident that Chrome Enterprise Premium provided our desired level of visibility, we rolled it out to several hundred users across various environments, including BYOD, Windows, and macOS. We deployed Safe Browsing and URL filtering for immediate threat protection, DLP rules to restrict copy/paste, downloads, and uploads on sensitive SaaS apps, and context-aware access to restrict application entry based on device posture.

The proof of concept succeeded across all criteria including consistent policy enforcement, measurable reduction in risky-site and risky-download events, minimal user friction, and a centralized dashboard to give our teams visibility into managed user activity.

The real decision moment came when we realized we could achieve a true Zero Trust posture. With Chrome Enterprise Premium as our backbone, access decisions now happen dynamically based on identity, device posture, and context. A teacher on a school-managed laptop enjoys seamless, full access. On a personal phone, that same educator can review materials without compromising security—downloads and clipboard sharing remain locked down. It delivers airtight data protection without disrupting daily instruction.

A simpler, stronger foundation

With Chrome Enterprise Premium, we replaced virtual desktops (VDIs) and fragmented security tools with built-in browser protection. Securing the browser itself means we no longer need to install heavy security software on every computer. This makes it easy to apply security policies to personal devices used by contractors and employees. Whether our team uses Windows, macOS, ChromeOS, iOS, or Android, we manage updates, policies, and audit reports from a single Google Admin console.

Chrome Enterprise Premium ensures we only grant access when it is safe. Every time someone tries to log in, we verify three things:

  • Identity: Is the user signed into their corporate account?
  • Device: Is the laptop or phone managed and secure?
  • Context: Where are they logging in from, and on what network?

We use Chrome Enterprise’s built-in features, such as Safe Browsing sandboxing and site isolation, and auto-updates to keep end users secure while they work on the web. These benefits plus Chrome Enterprise Premium prove that security does not have to slow down business. Employees work without security interruptions, and our IT team gets a single, clear audit trail across all devices. This helps us maintain high efficiency and supports our regulatory compliance efforts.

Want to know the latest from Google Cloud? Find it here in one handy location. Check back regularly for our newest updates, announcements, resources, events, learning opportunities, and more. 

  • Why your AI agent keeps forgetting: a 15 minute build on agent memoryAgents that resend the full conversation get slower and more expensive, and agents that keep nothing forget users between sessions. In the latest AI Agent Clinic episode, Google Cloud engineer Laxmi Harikumar and developer Miles Libbey add long term memory to a voice agent built with Agent Development Kit (ADK). They compare 4 memory options (flat prompting, RAG, knowledge graphs and Memory Bank in Gemini platform) and show 3 ways to keep context small. Watch the episode and get the code.
  • Cut background agent costs in half with the deferred tier on Gemini platformThe deferred service tier is generally available (GA) on the Gemini platform for the Interactions API, Agent Development Kit (ADK), and Deep Research. Running multi-hour background loops through synchronous real-time inference introduces unnecessary cost and triggers 429 resource exhaustion errors at peak. Static batch inference offers a 50% discount only when all prompts sit in a fixed input file upfront, which breaks dynamic tool loops. On the Gemini platform, the new deferred service tier brings batch economics to dynamic, stateful, multi-turn agents. Instead of competing with live chat traffic, the scheduler routes latency-tolerant agent turns to spare global capacity at half the cost.

    Set service_tier="deferred" in ADK RunConfig or client.interactions.create() across gemini-4-argon, gemini-4-carbon, gemini-3.x models, and gemini-deep-research-1.0. Read the guides for the

    • Managed queuing and state: During peak traffic, the platform queues and retries turns server-side with zero 429 errors. Pass previous_interaction_id to chain turns and retain warm prompt caches.
  • More frontier model choice on Google Cloud: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 and Meta’s Muse model series.

items.title: Scaling workforce productivity and upskilling in the agentic era
items.author: Brad HoffmanDirector, State, Local, Higher Ed CentralGoogle Public Sector
items.content:
As state and local agencies modernize to meet evolving public needs, leaders have an unprecedented opportunity to empower and elevate their teams. Modernizing public sector operations starts with giving dedicated public servants the right tools to thrive. By replacing repetitive administrative routines with intuitive, intelligent workflows, agencies can free their staff to do what they do best: focus on high-impact problem-solving, build rewarding careers, and deliver responsive, compassionate services to the residents and communities they serve.

Modernizing an agency workforce means transitioning employees from institutional systems to agentic platforms—redirecting their efforts away from manual administration and freeing up time for high-touch service delivery. By leveraging Google Cloud’s integrated stack to modernize daily operations, agency leaders can reliably meet regulatory requirements while creating the operational capacity to innovate, develop staff, and strengthen public trust.

Empowering municipal teams: The City of Los Angeles

Under the leadership of CIO Ted Ross, the City of Los Angeles addressed administrative constraints by deploying Google Workspace with Gemini across its entire 27,500-person municipal workforce. City employees now use agents to instantly synthesize large amounts of grant documents buried in silos and quickly rewrite public web copy for clearer readability. This digital companion allows city staff to step away from time-consuming administrative tasks and spend more time focusing on critical community service delivery, ensuring the city is operationally ready to host major global events like the 2028 Olympics and 2028 Paralympics.

Retaining regional talent: The University of Hawaii

The University of Hawaii needed a better way to keep local talent from leaving the islands. To build and retain regional talent, the university turned to BigQuery and Gemini—creating an automated, skills-first platform that helps match individuals with career opportunities. This solution maps student and faculty capabilities, matches individuals to academic roles and public research projects, and helps retain top talent.

Overcoming timeline constraints: The Indiana Department of Transportation

The Indiana Department of Transportation was issued an urgent executive mandate requiring a comprehensive review of complex legal contracts within a strict 30-day window. The agency deployed Gemini to securely ingest, parse, and analyze the state’s contract repositories. The automated system successfully isolated key legal parameters, saving 360 hours of highly skilled engineering labor and meeting the strict deadline.

Scaling document ingestion: State of Maryland

A similar transformation occurred within Maryland’s state agencies, where caseworkers navigating complex public benefits documentation spent hours indexing files and searching manual handbooks to find specific clause requirements. Maryland deployed Gemini and Gemini Notebook across its 40,000-person state workforce, establishing a secure framework to index and interact with state benefits compliance manuals. Caseworkers can now run plain-language queries to retrieve policy directives in seconds, drastically reducing the administrative processing times for residents.

Celebrating the builders of the agentic enterprise

Giving the public sector workforce a secure starting point for enterprise workflows streamlines routine processes, creating the space for employees to expand their skills and lead strategic mission priorities. To discover how your agency can empower its workforce, register to watch our Google Public Sector Summit on-demand.
